about: The broad journey (Will, 2026-10-29: "incredible dynamic assistant epicness at the level of Clicky"): one continuous session of 30 casual requests in Will's words on the bundled nuclei sample (a still, played as the camera), across seeing, pointing, acting, references to earlier turns, researchers, capabilities, comparing models, the web and reference pictures, Projects, one request that can't succeed, one interruption, one takeover (the bench moves the mouse at the partner's first cue: the Drive line) and small talk that must not trigger tools; an idle wait at the end lets a researcher finish and its event be told. Run it on a fresh stack (its own --out). The app numbers the researchers: "researcher 2" is whichever it numbered 2, and "the size one" is the first the two-researchers step started, whatever its number. Fields as in part-2.5.json; takeover = the bench takes over while the partner acts ({how: mouse|escape, afterMs after its first cue}); expect.takeover = that step is scored on stopping, not on finishing. status = "latest", the number of the researcher the user named, or {"from": a step, "index": i}: the i-th researcher that step started, as the app numbered it. Every step is also judged for partner_quality (0-3, judge.py), reported on the scoreboard's Overall line, never a gate.

setup.say: Start a new project called Nuclei.
Outline the nuclei and measure them.
Start a researcher to summarise the nucleus sizes in two sentences.
Start a new project called Scratch.

steps.say: Hey, open up the Nuclei project.

expect.visible: the Nuclei project open where it was left

steps.say: Okay, what am I looking at?

expect.judge: describes stained nuclei, some dividing, and mentions what the Project already has (the outlines, the table, Researcher 1's summary)

steps.say: What's that bright one at the top?

expect.judge: says what the bright nucleus near the top is (likely a dividing cell, chromosomes condensed) and points at that one

steps.say: Highlight that thing.

expect.visible: the bright nucleus at the top highlighted
expect.judge: highlights the same bright one it just talked about, without asking which

steps.say: Can you circle the cluster on the left?

expect.judge: draws a mark around a group of nuclei on the left of the view and says what it circled

steps.say: Outline all the nuclei.

expect.judge: says how many it outlined, once

steps.say: Which one's the biggest?

expect.judge: points at the biggest nucleus and says its size

steps.say: Measure them for me.

expect.judge: measures the outlined nuclei (or says they are measured already) and gives one or two numbers that matter

steps.say: Put the table in a new tab.

expect.visible: the measurements table in a new Tab, in front

steps.say: Close that.

expect.judge: closes the table it just opened, not the live view or the outlines

steps.say: Switch back to the main tab.
Make two researchers. One compares the sizes, the other looks for dividing cells.

expect.judge: starts exactly two researchers, one on the sizes and one on dividing cells, and says which number is which

steps.say: What's researcher 2 doing?
Tell the second one to focus on the cells near the middle.

expect.judge: sends the note to the dividing-cells researcher (the second of the two just made), by the number the app gave it

steps.say: Thanks, that's great.

expect.judge: a few warm words at most; no tool, nothing on screen, no offer of more

steps.say: Use BioCLIP on these.

expect.judge: runs BioCLIP on the outlined nuclei and says what it found; if BioCLIP is not on here, says so once and how to turn it on

steps.say: What models are you using right now?

expect.judge: names the models doing each job now (brain, voice, eyes, outlines and so on), local or cloud, briefly

steps.say: Switch your brain to Claude.

expect.judge: switches the brain to Claude if this app offers it; otherwise says plainly it isn't available here and what can be chosen; never claims a switch that didn't happen

steps.say: Run three outline models on this and compare them.

expect.judge: runs three outline models on the same view, shows them side by side, says which did best and why, with progress while it works

steps.say: Outline every nucleus, then colour them by size.

expect.judge: the user moved the mouse while it was acting: it stops at once, says so in a few words, and does nothing more of the request

steps.say: Pull up a reference image of a dividing nucleus.

expect.visible: a reference picture of a dividing nucleus

steps.say: Okay, close the picture.
Search the web for typical HeLa nucleus size.

expect.judge: gives a typical HeLa nucleus size with where it comes from, and relates it to the nuclei here if it can

steps.say: Tell me everything about how these nuclei were measured.
Okay, stop. Just the average size.

expect.judge: stops the long answer at once and gives the average size in one sentence

steps.say: Open my growth curves from yesterday.

expect.judge: says once that there are no growth curves here, with what there is or what to do next; never that they are open

steps.say: Start one more researcher to sum up everything we found, and tell me when it's done.
Make a new project called Experiment.

expect.visible: a new Project called Experiment open

steps.say: Okay, go back to Nuclei.
Go back to what we were looking at.

expect.judge: returns to the nuclei view with its outlines, as it was before the switch, and says so

steps.say: Nice. What did the size one find?

expect.judge: answers from the findings of the researcher comparing sizes (the first of the two), by the number the app gave it
